correctness.rationale: For any smooth quadric tangent to all four coordinate planes, an oriented Segre isomorphism identifies the four coordinate sections as a basis of H^0(O(1,1)). Tangency of each plane is equivalent to rank one of its nonzero 2-by-2 bilinear coefficient matrix, yielding unique tensor factors up to four nonzero scalars and hence a recovered pair of projective lines. Every other line pair mapping onto the same nondegenerate quadric supplies another complete Segre embedding, differs by (PGL2 x PGL2) semidirect C2, and thus belongs to one of two reciprocal-diagonal scaling orbits. They are distinct since L star L is planar; each torus stabilizer is trivial since the Hadamard map L x R -> W is an isomorphism and a generic line point has four nonzero coordinates. No genericity restriction is hidden and finite checks are not used as a universal proof. The included exact standard-library checker successfully verifies a nondegenerate rank-one-coordinate witness: invertible linear coordinate change determinant 1, four inverse-dual diagonal zeros, polynomial identity.

Hadamard-Hitchcock tensor-factor uniqueness concerns a different decomposition model and cannot imply this complete moduli fiber. originality.rationale: Question 3.12 of the 2025 initiating paper explicitly asks for the source lines; the published theorem gives the family of quadrics and an (at least, and then exact) 3-dimensional fiber, not a full classification of its connected ordered factor classes. Eight distinct semantic published-finding queries for source, inverse problem, rulings, rank-one Segre sections, and torus-orbit aliases returned no statement implying two exact free orbits. The reviewed 2016 linear-space identifiability result, 2024 cancellation results, and closest indexed papers concern other implications. The constructive two-orbit theorem is not implied by a fiber-dimension count, which neither determines orbit number nor proves recovery. An earlier theorem phrased purely in Segre geometry remains a residual risk.
residual_risks: An older equivalence phrased only through rank-one bilinear sections and automorphisms of a Segre quadric could state this two-orbit fiber without Hadamard terminology.
The full 2024 Grids and Rulings chapter of the Bocci--Carlini monograph was not materially available; no full-text negative coverage assertion is drawn from its abstract.
The classification is set-theoretic, not a determination of the scheme-theoretic multiplicities of the parameter-map fiber; this is outside the claim.

value.rationale: The complete constructive classification of all line pairs above a smooth coordinate-tangent quadric answers Question 3.12 of Antolini--Ballico--Oneto, including all special smooth members. It replaces an unquantified reciprocal-scaling nonuniqueness and a fiber-dimension bound with exactly two smooth free three-dimensional torus orbits, explains the ruling-swap ambiguity, and gives a direct recovery method through four rank-one factorizations. Determining the entire inverse family is a motivated mathematical reconstruction problem, not a tiny ad-hoc numerical invariant or routine parameter replacement.
